A_target.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Directed Graph|directed graph]] with [[Definition:Adjacency Matrix|adjacency matrix]] $A$ over the [[Definition:Boolean Semiring|Boolean semiring]] $\struct {\set {0, 1}, \lor, \land}$.
Then for all $k \ge 1$:
:$\paren {A^k}_{i j} = 1 \iff$ there is a [[Definition:Walk (Graph Theory)|walk]] of length $k$ from $i$ to $j$

B_source.statement:
Let $A$ be the weighted [[Definition:Adjacency Matrix|adjacency matrix]] of a [[Definition:Directed Graph|directed graph]] over a [[Definition:Commutative Ring|commutative ring]].
Then:
:$\displaystyle \paren {A^k}_{i j} = \sum_{i = v_0 \to v_1 \to \cdots \to v_k = j} \prod_{t \mathop = 1}^k A_{v_{t - 1} v_t}$
the sum over all [[Definition:Walk (Graph Theory)|walks]] of length $k$ from $i$ to $j$.

validity_conditions: the Boolean values with or and and must form a semiring, which they do, so associativity of matrix product is inherited
the semiring lacks additive inverses, so any argument using subtraction or determinants does not transfer
idempotence of disjunction is what turns counting into existence testing
proof_plan: Replace the coefficient ring by the [[Definition:Boolean Semiring|Boolean semiring]], with $\lor$ as addition and $\land$ as multiplication.

$\struct {\set {0, 1}, \lor, \land}$ satisfies the [[Definition:Semiring|semiring axioms]].
These are all that is used to prove [[Matrix Multiplication is Associative|associativity of matrix multiplication]].

The walk-counting proof by [[Principle of Mathematical Induction|induction]] on $k$ goes through verbatim:
:$\displaystyle \paren {A^{k + 1} }_{i j} = \bigvee_l \paren {\paren {A^k}_{i l} \land A_{l j} }$
with sums of products becoming disjunctions of conjunctions.
Hence $\paren {A^k}_{i j} = 1$ {{iff}} at least one walk of length $k$ from $i$ to $j$ exists.

Results relying on subtraction, such as those involving the [[Definition:Determinant of Matrix|determinant]], do not transfer, since the semiring has no [[Definition:Additive Inverse|additive inverses]].
{{qed}}
